hook.title: One .tsx. A website, an iPhone app and an Android app.
hook.lede: Pyreon compiles your components to SwiftUI and Jetpack Compose views, so no JavaScript engine runs your UI on the device, and the same source server-renders on the web. The native targets are experimental; the web side is the mature part.

proof.label: canonical primitives (`Stack`, `Text`, `Field`, `Select`, `Scroll`…) that compile to SwiftUI and Compose views and render DOM on the web
under your UI on the device: the generated app is SwiftUI or Compose code (a WebView appears only where you host one)
required device lanes in CI: XCUITest on an iOS Simulator and Compose instrumented tests on an Android emulator

table.title: Pyreon Native and React Native, line by line.
table.note: Pyreon's native targets are experimental; React Native and Expo run production apps at scale. This table follows the repo's own comparison page and is honest about where Expo is ahead.

rows.pyreon: Generated SwiftUI and Compose: the platform's own widgets.
rows.rival: Platform widgets through React Native's renderer; Expo UI adds SwiftUI and Compose components.

rows.pyreon: None: the app is a native binary.
rows.source: docs/src/content/docs/compare-app-frameworks.md (we publish no speed or size number for this)

rows.pyreon: First-class: SSR, SSG, ISR, islands, SPA.
rows.rival: react-native-web and Expo Router web; SSR is newer and still maturing.

rows.pyreon: Signals lower to `@State` / `@Observable` in SwiftUI and `mutableStateOf` in Compose.
A narrow, declarative subset compiles; the rest gets a named warning almost always.
Not possible for native logic: it is compiled.
rows.rival: EAS Update ships JavaScript fixes between store reviews.

rows.pyreon: First-party hooks for common cases plus a `useNativeModule` bridge you write.
rows.rival: The largest catalog (Expo SDK plus community).

rows.pyreon: Web: yes. Native: a rebuild per change, about 3 s warm with `pyreon-native dev`.

code.title: The same todo screen, twice.
code.caption: On the right, `<Stack>` becomes a `VStack` and a `Column`, `<Field>` a `TextField`, and `<Scroll>` around `<For>` a lazy list on both platforms. The same file renders DOM on the web.

rival.label: React Native

pyreon.label: Pyreon (web, iOS, Android)

code.checked: Pyreon side: typechecked against the repo; lowered by the native compiler with the first-party plugins to SwiftUI (`VStack`, `TextField`, `ScrollView { LazyVStack }`) and Compose (`Column`, `TextField`, `LazyColumn`) with zero warnings; the Swift output passed the repo's SwiftUI typecheck. React Native side: written against the React Native core components; not compiled here.

items.instead: Signals and `computed`; the screen component runs once.
`<For each by>` inside `<Scroll>`, which becomes a lazy list on iOS and Android.

pickTheOther.title: When to pick React Native or Expo
items: You ship logic fixes over the air between store reviews: that is EAS Update, and compiled native code cannot do it.
You depend on many third-party native SDKs and have no time to write bridges.
Your app is graphics-heavy or animation-led (Reanimated, Skia).
You must ship a production store app next quarter: Pyreon's native targets are experimental.

migrate.title: Coming from React Native and Expo?
migrate.text: There is no compat layer for React Native. The guide maps `View`, `Text`, `Pressable`, Expo Router and the `expo-*` modules to Pyreon, and lists what does not carry over.
